evidence:
Dimension weights: task/tests/scoring.toml is identical to the template ([gates] render=0.0, constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2; [floors] functional=0.05), and score.py is byte-identical to the template. Functionality (0.6) outweighs polish+visual (0.4), and pure style (visual) is capped at 0.2 of the reward. No weight key appears inside any [judge] block; gates carry no reward mass.

Per-criterion weights (tomllib parse): functional has 43 binary criteria totalling 58.5. The highest weights (2.5 each, 4.3% of functional) go to the hardest public promises: hro_stale_refused (refusal of a stale move naming who changed the card, instruction.md para 2), hro_live_board (other people's moves within 15 s without reload) and hro_candidate_private (no notes/rejection reason/other candidates leaked). Next tier, weight 2: bulk all-or-none, undo restores, undo conflict, refused put-back, thread paging, unread counts, scrolled-up behaviour and drafts. The lowest weights (0.5) go to hro_job_open and hro_add_candidate, which gates/constraints hro_gate_shared already requires (open a job, add a candidate, independent readback), and to narrow edge or link rows (hro_reject_hired, hro_undo_full, hro_activity_refusals, hro_candidate_linked). Because a gated app must already do the basics, it earns little extra for them, and most weight sits on concurrency, permission and conversation rules. That is consistent with the workbook annotation (functional 60 percent; each dimension sets its own per-criterion weights) and with skill line 28.

Polish (5 binary criteria, total 12) grades behaviour, not styling: live board/thread updates that keep the open card, typed note, cursor and scroll (3 + 3); keeping your place when earlier messages load (2); recovery from a failed send (1.5); draft survives sign-out and is isolated from other users (2.5). Each traces to instruction.md paragraphs 3-5 and hireops_rules.md lines 118-124. Visual has 5 likert criteria (points=5) at 1.2 each, so equal weight across typography, colour, layout, hierarchy and consistency.

Maximum non-functional contribution (sanity check from quality-checks.md line 179): a pretty but barely working app passes both gates. It then needs functional above 0.05 (for example add_candidate 0.5 + add_email_rules 1 + restart 1.5 = 3/58.5 = 0.051), giving at most 0.6*0.051 + 0.2*visual(1.0) + 0.2*polish(~0, because the polish rows need working live updates and drafts) ≈ 0.23. A fully functional but plain app scores at least 0.6, plus any visual credit. A gated app with functional at or below 0.05 gets 0. So style cannot outrank working behaviour through the weights.

Adversarial attempts:
(a) Plausible broken app that the weights might over-reward: a styled board with working gates and add/open, but no concurrency, undo, live updates or conversations. It is capped near 0.23 as computed above, so the weights do not inflate it.
(b) Conforming alternative that the weights might under-reward: an app that preserves focus/drafts differently but correctly. Those behaviours are public (hireops_rules.md lines 84-85 and 118-124), and the binary criteria accept alternatives (for example 'refuses before the card moves ... also passes' in hro_refused_put_back). No weight concentrates on a golden-only default.

Scope note: this row is an analytical weight review. The raw-evidence-index scope says measured reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/model scores are absent. That measurement gap belongs to the runtime/ranking rows (#42 and the pipeline runtime records) and is not waived here. No Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
